name: 01-python-the-race-and-the-query-in-the-lessons-words
why: Both findings name the broken idea in the words of the lesson sentences the key cites and never use a pattern's name. The first says the stock check is out of date by the time the update runs and that check and update must happen under one lock, which is what the linked sentences teach about a check on shared state: the race is found. The second says the sku is pasted into the query text and must be passed apart from the statement as data, which is the idea of the linked sentences on queries: the injection is found. Under the design's rule a finding that names the broken idea in the lesson's words is found, not only one that names the pattern. Creating a lock for each call would guard nothing, since no two calls would share it, and the code is right to create it once: false positive. The off-by-one in restock_gaps is not mentioned: missed.

key.consequence: A caller who controls the sku can end the quoted string and add SQL of their own, reading or changing any table.

fix.before: f"SELECT quantity FROM stock WHERE sku = '{sku}'"

key.explanation: stock() puts the sku into the SQL text with an f-string, so a sku that contains a quote can rewrite the query. Pass it as a bound parameter and the database never reads it as SQL.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the bound parameter with an f-string, and the clean code binds it.

sentences.text: A query is a program the database runs, so values must never be pasted into its text.
Send values to the database apart from the statement, as parameters, and it will treat them as data whatever they contain.

key.consequence: Two requests can both pass the stock check before either one updates it, so the same units are sold twice and the stock goes negative.
key.explanation: reserve() checks the stock before it takes the lock, so the check and the update are not one step. Two workers can both see enough stock and both take it. Hold the lock across the check and the update.

judged.reason: The edit moves the stock check out of the lock that guards the update, which the clean code holds across both.

sentences.text: A check on shared state means nothing if the state can change before the action that depends on it.
Hold the lock across the check and the action so that the two happen as one step.

key.consequence: On the last pass history[i + 1] is past the end of the list, so any call with a non-empty history raises IndexError.
key.explanation: The loop reads history[i + 1], so it has to stop one short of the end. Running over every index reads past the last element.

judged.reason: The edit drops the - 1 from the loop bound, so the last pass indexes past the end.

review.text: By the time this method takes the lock another worker may already have reserved the units this check just counted, so the check is out of date when the update runs. The check and the update have to happen under the same lock, as one step.

The sku is pasted into the text of the query, so a sku that contains a quote is read by the database as part of the statement. Pass it as a parameter, apart from the statement, so that it is only ever data.
Create the lock inside reserve so that each call gets its own.
